content:
CarPlay can make any car more comfortable and convenient. However, the original experience is not always perfect.

Some car models still require a wired connection, while others don't have CarPlay at all, let alone charging and cooling your iPhone during long journeys.

Fortunately, improving these aspects doesn't require a big investment. From wireless CarPlay and MagSafe charging to cable management and even adding a complete display to an older car, these affordable accessories can take care of everything.

Converting Wired CarPlay to Wireless

If your vehicle already supports wired CarPlay, the Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 can eliminate the cables while retaining the vehicle's touchscreen steering wheel controls, knob buttons, built-in microphone, and original sound system.

This compact adapter comes with USB-A and USB-C ports. After the initial pairing, it will automatically reconnect every time you start the car. It also supports wireless Android Auto for Android 11 or above, making it particularly practical for vehicles shared by iPhone and Android users.

One thing to note: this adapter requires factory-installed wired CarPlay and cannot add this function to cars that don't have CarPlay.

The Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 is priced at $43.99, with free shipping for Prime members.

Adding CarPlay to Almost Any Older Car

If your vehicle doesn't have CarPlay, a portable display is often the simplest upgrade solution. The Krunia 9.26-inch portable CarPlay screen is priced at $89.99, adding wireless CarPlay without removing the original audio system.

The screen supports Bluetooth, AUX, and FM audio connections, and is compatible with Siri, Android Auto, and OTA firmware updates. It also comes with a reversing camera, but installation requires routing cables to the rear of the car.

For those who want to enjoy CarPlay without replacing the original head unit, this is a rather attractive compromise.

Installing a Permanent CarPlay Head Unit

A portable display may not suit all dashboards. For a more polished permanent solution, the BVCP9700A from BOSS Audio is an affordably priced double-DIN head unit, featuring a 7-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, and reversing camera support.

The head unit is priced at $164.99. However, buyers should confirm compatibility with their vehicle before ordering. Dashboard installation kits, wiring harnesses, steering wheel control adapters, or professional installation fees may increase the overall cost.

Charging While Cooling Your iPhone

Wireless charging, navigation operation, sunlight exposure, combined with a hot dashboard, create a rather harsh combination for your iPhone. The ESR CryoBoost MagSafe car charger features a built-in cooling fan that solves this problem. It combines a magnetic vent or dashboard mount, wireless charging, and active cooling. Priced at $29.99, it's especially suitable for drivers using wireless CarPlay who still want to charge their iPhone during long journeys.

Replacing Charging with a Simpler MagSafe Mount

Not every drive requires wireless charging. The standard ESR MagSafe car mount can hold your iPhone on the dashboard or air vent without additional charging cables.

Priced at $15.99, it comes with a metal ring sticker for use with iPhones or cases that don't have built-in magnets. In hot climates, charging generates additional heat, so this mount might be a more suitable choice.

Replacing Unreliable CarPlay Cables

Many CarPlay issues stem from aging cables or poor connections. The Anker Nano USB-A to USB-C CarPlay cable features a braided design, providing stable data transmission for newer iPhones with USB-C ports, priced at $11.99.

Users with iPhone 14 or older models can opt for the Anker PowerLine Flow USB-A to Lightning cable, priced at $17.99.

Adding Fast Charging for a Better Experience

The USB port running wired CarPlay often charges slowly. The Anker 323 car charger plugs into the 12V cigarette lighter socket, providing one USB-C port and one USB-A port.

Priced at $14.99, it's an affordable way to charge passengers' phones or power other accessories without affecting the vehicle's CarPlay connection—and when used with wireless CarPlay, it can also speed up the phone's own charging.

Tidying Up Your Setup

A pack of adhesive cable clips priced at $6.99 can make installing a portable CarPlay display or wired phone mount look much neater. These clips can route cables along the edges of the dashboard, keeping them away from the gear shift, pedals, and cup holders.

CarPlay doesn't require buying a new car, nor does it require an elaborate audio system upgrade. Depending on your vehicle's existing features, spending from $12 on a better cable to around $90 on a complete portable display can make daily use much more convenient.

Want to make the most of CarPlay? Check out 9to5Mac's continuously updated list of over 120 iPhone apps that support CarPlay.
